newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros secessionists elect leader as "president".
newsitem.headline: Comoros secessionists elect leader as "president".

text.p: Comoros secessionists on the island of Anjouan said they elected on Tuesday their 75-year-old leader Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim as "president" of their breakaway state in the Indian Ocean archipelago.
They told a news conference in the Anjouan capital of Mutsamudu that Fatima Abdere Mahe was appointed deputy president and Charikane Ahmed was put in charge of coordination with the president.

"Other portfolios will be filled in the coming hours," Charikane told Reuters by telephone from Anjouan, adding that former Comoron prime minister Mohamed Abdou Madi, 41, had been put in charge of foreign affairs for the new state of Anjouan.
"This is a provisional government," he added.

Ibrahim is a former Koranic teacher and jeweller who was arrested by Comoran authorities for five days last month. He and three other secessionist leaders were freed after troops fired on demonstrators.

The Comoro Islands, with a population of 190,000, became independent from France in 1975. Residents of Anjouan, Comoros' second island, say independence has brought only poverty, civil strife and numerous coups, and want to return to French rule.
Anjouan's poverty contrasts with the relative prosperity of the island of Mayotte, which voted to remain French in 1975.
France has denounced the secessionists, saying the Anjouan situation is serious and could destabilise the whole region.
Comoran President Mohamed Taki said last Friday the islands would be given more autonomy and would be divided into communes.
Youths in the Anjouan capital Mutsamudu rebuilt street barricades after the speech amid rumours of imminent military intervention to seize government buildings, witnesses said.

Three people including a gendarme were killed on July 14 as demonstrators who want Anjouan to return to French rule or be independent clashed with security forces. Several were killed in March clashes.
The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) appealed on Monday for calm on Anjouan and said it would send a special envoy to the Comoro Islands mandated to talk to both the government and secessionists.
The French government on Monday again rejected demands by the Anjouan separatists to return to its rule, saying a solution to the whole crisis should respect the archipelego's integrity.
